items.title: Kinjal Kaur and Krishna Aarya Trivedi, WRDSB Student Trustees
notes:
K. Kaur and K. Aarya Trivedi provided a presentation to Council on a Grand River Transit student rate. A copy of their presentation is attached to the agenda. They requested that Council direct staff to determine the feasibility and implementation of a universal student/youth fare for Grand River Transit, considering an expansion to the Affordable Transit Program, or the creation of a new program, and report back to the Council. They noted that attendance and overall student mobility would be improved with affordable transit for students. They emphasized that this is not a request for increased service. 

Council directed staff to coordinate with the delegates and to incorporate the recommendations within the staff transit review.

items.title: Krista Straus, Wilmot
notes: K. Straus expressed concerns related to water taking in the Township of Wilmot and that there has been historical repetition of water taking that resulted in impacting the water levels of private wells. She noted that in the 1970s the wetlands were also impacted by water taking. She requested that Council reconsider decisions related to groundwater specifically with the development of the Wilmot Land Assembly. A copy of their presentation is attached to the agenda.

items.title: Margaret Johnston, Kitchener
notes:
M. Johnston expressed concern related to the proposed delay of the Mooregate housing project. She provided lived experience accounts received from various Mooregate residents that expressed their disappointment in the delay of the Mooregate housing project. A copy of their presentation is attached to the agenda.

She requested that Council defeat the recommended motion related to the Mooregate housing project listed under item 12.2.3. and that staff provide ongoing communications with continuous meetings and improved signage. 

Responding to Council, M. Johnston recommended that community communication needs to be expanded to include various languages, regular updates to the engage page, and generally maintaining the sense of community establish at Mooregate.

Peter Sweeney, Commissioner of Community Services, explained that meetings with staff were offered to Mooregate residents.

Council recessed at 8:37 p.m.

items.title: Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee - April 7, 2026
Community and Health Services Committee Summary - April 7, 2026
Board of Health Update
notes:
Dr. Hsiu-Li Wang, Commissioner Public Health & Paramedic Services/Medical Officer of Health, provided an update on vaccine requirements related to the Immunization of School Pupils Act (1990). 

H. Wang reminded Council and the public that the deadline to submit immunization records for elementary school students is May 4, 2026 at 4:30, with suspensions taking effect on May 7, 2026.

H. Wang stated that between January and February of 2026, 9,234 notices of incomplete immunization records were sent out. In early April of 2026, 7,065 suspension orders were sent out. H. Wang stated that these numbers are aligned with historical trends.  

H. Wang stated the current number of elementary school students with incomplete immunization records is 4,248.

H. Wang encouraged parents and guardians to update vaccine records as soon as possible to avoid suspension. 

Received for information.

items.title: PDL-CAS-26-009, Remuneration Recommendation
notes:
Tim Brubacher, Regional Clerk/Council and Administration Services, provided a brief overview of the recommendation in the report PDL-CAS-26-009, Remuneration Recommendation. He highlighted that the recommendation is based on the external consultant recommendations.

Responding to Council, T. Brubacher clarified the scope of the external consultant was to assess remuneration, medical benefits, and staff support, which is why childcare wasn't included. 

Council discussed and debated various amendments to the proposed motion, including the removal of the proposed FTE for the Regional Chair's office and an increase to compensation for Standing Committee Chairs.

Motion for Committee of the Whole to Rise and Council Resume
Motion To Adopt Proceedings of Committee of the Whole
Motions where notice has been provided
Councillor J. Gowing
notes:
J. Gowing introduced his motion to Council and expressed the importance of proactively addressing housing needs.

Council discussed and debated the motion, specifically asking questions about the municipal housing corporation managed by the Region known as Region of Waterloo Community Housing Inc. (ROWCHI).

items.title: Councillor C. James
notes:
C. James provided a description of her motion and explained how caregiving responsibilities can create a structural barrier to participation in muncipal governance. 

Responding to Council, C. James confirmed that there are existing models for childcare reimbursement in other municipalities that can be referenced. 

Council discussed and debated the motion expressing both support and concern, specifically with the cost of reimbursement and difficulties with care coverage during atypical hours.

items.title: Other Business
notes:
D. Craig directed staff to provide an update on the City of Cambridge access to GOTrain services which should provide information on the timeline and the equity between area municipality. 

M. Goetzke confirmed that the Cambridge to Guelph GO project was forwarded to the Ministry of Transportation for consideration for CPTF funding. 

D. McCabe requested clarification on the Region of Waterloo's leave policy for employees serving as military reservists. Kate Konopka, Commissioner of Human Resources, confirmed that staff will provide a report on a reservist policy.

motions.text: As Amended: Municipal Housing Corporation – Strategic Review WHEREAS the Region continues to experience increasing housing pressures, including chronic homelessness and sustained demand for emergency shelter services; AND WHEREAS expanding access to permanent supportive and affordable housing is a key component of improving housing stability and reducing long-term reliance on emergency systems; AND WHEREAS municipalities across Ontario have established Municipal Housing Corporations as strategic tools to support the development, delivery, and long-term management of housing; AND WHEREAS such a model may provide the Region with additional capacity to deliver housing, leverage external funding, and support long-term financial sustainability; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT: Staff be directed to report back to Community and Health Services Committee by Q2 2027 on the feasibility and potential role of establishing a Municipal Housing Corporation for the Region. That the review consider how such a corporation could support a phased approach to housing delivery , including an initial focus on supportive housing, Waterloo Region Housing Revitalization Plan priority projects and broader opportunities for affordable and mixed-income housing over time. That staff report on governance, financial, and operational considerations , including potential approaches to capitalization, partnerships, and long-term asset management. That the report identify potential benefits, risks, and implementation considerations , including opportunities to leverage federal and provincial housing funding programs. AND FURTHER THAT: The review include consideration of how such a model could contribute to improved housing outcomes, including reducing chronic homelessness and pressures on emergency shelter systems.
motions.text_html:
As Amended:

Municipal Housing Corporation – Strategic Review

WHEREAS the Region continues to experience increasing housing pressures, including chronic homelessness and sustained demand for emergency shelter services;

AND WHEREAS expanding access to permanent supportive and affordable housing is a key component of improving housing stability and reducing long-term reliance on emergency systems;

AND WHEREAS municipalities across Ontario have established Municipal Housing Corporations as strategic tools to support the development, delivery, and long-term management of housing;

AND WHEREAS such a model may provide the Region with additional capacity to deliver housing, leverage external funding, and support long-term financial sustainability;

THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT:

  1. Staff be directed to report back to Community and Health Services Committee by Q2 2027 on the feasibility and potential role of establishing a Municipal Housing Corporation for the Region.
  2. That the review consider how such a corporation could support a phased approach to housing delivery, including an initial focus on supportive housing, Waterloo Region Housing Revitalization Plan priority projects and broader opportunities for affordable and mixed-income housing over time.
  3. That staff report on governance, financial, and operational considerations, including potential approaches to capitalization, partnerships, and long-term asset management.
  4. That the report identify potential benefits, risks, and implementation considerations, including opportunities to leverage federal and provincial housing funding programs.

AND FURTHER THAT:

The review include consideration of how such a model could contribute to improved housing outcomes, including reducing chronic homelessness and pressures on emergency shelter systems.

motions.text: WHEREAS elected officials are required to attend Council, committee, and other official meetings that frequently occur during evenings, weekends, or outside standard child care and caregiving hours; and WHEREAS the lack of affordable, flexible childcare and caregiving options is a documented barrier to participation in municipal governance, disproportionately impacting women, single parents, individuals with caregiving responsibilities for children or elder family members, and others with dependent care obligations, including persons with disabilities; and WHEREAS in Ontario, there is no standardized legislative framework supporting caregiving leave for municipal elected officials, and no province-wide mechanism to recognize caregiving-related interruptions as a protected status in elected office, resulting in a gap in supports for those balancing public service with caregiving responsibilities; and WHEREAS the removal of systemic barriers to seeking and holding elected office is essential to ensuring municipal councils are representative of the communities they serve; and WHEREAS a growing number of Canadian municipalities have adopted reimbursement-based policies (not allowances) for childcare and caregiving expenses incurred by elected officials in the course of their official duties, including the City of Sarnia, Ontario, and municipalities in Alberta such as Banff and Okotoks; and WHEREAS such policies are structured as cost-recovery mechanisms that reimburse actual, reasonable expenses directly related to the performance of official municipal responsibilities and are distinct from remuneration or personal benefits. THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED THAT: Council directs staff to prepare and bring forward amendments to the elected officials’ expense reimbursement policy to explicitly include reimbursement for reasonable and necessary childcare and/or caregiving expenses (including elder care) incurred while performing official duties at Council, committee, and other approved municipal business; and Council further directs staff to report back with a proposed policy framework that includes: A jurisdictional scan of comparable Canadian municipal policies, including the City of Sarnia and municipalities in Alberta such as Banff and Okotoks; and A review of legislative authority and legal considerations under the Municipal Act, 2001 and applicable expense by-laws; Clearly defined eligibility criteria, documentation requirements, cost controls, and transparency and accountability measures; and A detailed analysis of the financial implications. Council directs that, upon approval, the finalized policy be formally shared with Area Municipalities, the Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO), and the Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM) as a best practice to support inclusive and representative local governance.
motions.text_html:
WHEREAS elected officials are required to attend Council, committee, and other official meetings that frequently occur during evenings, weekends, or outside standard child care and caregiving hours; and

WHEREAS the lack of affordable, flexible childcare and caregiving options is a documented barrier to participation in municipal governance, disproportionately impacting women, single parents, individuals with caregiving responsibilities for children or elder family members, and others with dependent care obligations, including persons with disabilities; and

WHEREAS in Ontario, there is no standardized legislative framework supporting caregiving leave for municipal elected officials, and no province-wide mechanism to recognize caregiving-related interruptions as a protected status in elected office, resulting in a gap in supports for those balancing public service with caregiving responsibilities; and

WHEREAS the removal of systemic barriers to seeking and holding elected office is essential to ensuring municipal councils are representative of the communities they serve; and

WHEREAS a growing number of Canadian municipalities have adopted reimbursement-based policies (not allowances) for childcare and caregiving expenses incurred by elected officials in the course of their official duties, including the City of Sarnia, Ontario, and municipalities in Alberta such as Banff and Okotoks; and

WHEREAS such policies are structured as cost-recovery mechanisms that reimburse actual, reasonable expenses directly related to the performance of official municipal responsibilities and are distinct from remuneration or personal benefits.

THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED THAT:

  1. Council directs staff to prepare and bring forward amendments to the elected officials’ expense reimbursement policy to explicitly include reimbursement for reasonable and necessary childcare and/or caregiving expenses (including elder care) incurred while performing official duties at Council, committee, and other approved municipal business; and

  2. Council further directs staff to report back with a proposed policy framework that includes:
    • A jurisdictional scan of comparable Canadian municipal policies, including the City of Sarnia and municipalities in Alberta such as Banff and Okotoks; and
    • A review of legislative authority and legal considerations under the Municipal Act, 2001 and applicable expense by-laws;
    • Clearly defined eligibility criteria, documentation requirements, cost controls, and transparency and accountability measures; and
    • A detailed analysis of the financial implications.
  3. Council directs that, upon approval, the finalized policy be formally shared with Area Municipalities, the Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO), and the Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM) as a best practice to support inclusive and representative local governance.
